今天的主题：医疗健康和科学研究。这组词是雅思高频话题：大作文常考「政府该不该多投钱做医学研究」「科技进步对健康的影响」；阅读里科普文章常出现 research、trial、breakthrough、significant 这类词；口语 Part 1 的 Health，Part 3「科学发展对生活的影响」都能直接用。今天是第 4 周最后一天，也是打基础阶段的最后一天，明天开始进入强化期。

例句

  • Scientists have made a major breakthrough in cancer research.（科学家在癌症研究上取得了重大突破。）
  • The new vaccine is still being tested in clinical trials.（新疫苗还在临床试验阶段。）
  • Regular exercise can help prevent many common diseases.（经常锻炼能帮助预防很多常见疾病。）
  • This treatment is more effective and has fewer side effects than existing ones.（这种疗法比现有疗法更有效，副作用也更少。）
  • There has been significant progress in medical technology over the past twenty years.（过去二十年医疗技术有了显著进步。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 research、breakthrough、significant 写一句「政府应该资助医学研究」，大作文能直接用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Could vaccines cure cancer?（疫苗能治愈癌症吗？）。这集讲一种新的皮肤癌疫苗：它不是用来预防的，而是病人切除肿瘤后，根据每个人肿瘤细胞的突变专门定制，帮免疫系统提前「认出」癌细胞，防止复发。科学家说这可能是一次突破，但还要更多试验。中间有两段真实采访录音（主持人 Tom Whipple 和生物学家 Anne Willis），专业词多一点，所以生词卡和原文注释给得比较全。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：根据世界卫生组织，全世界最常见的癌症是哪种？a) 肺癌 b) 皮肤癌 c) 胃癌。顺便听出：现有的哪两种癌症疗法副作用多？新疫苗是给什么时候的病人用的？2024 年这种癌症全世界大约有多少病例？
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Anne Willis 讲疫苗原理那段（"So, cancer cells are very different from normal cells..."）术语最多，可以先读懂中文再听。
  4. 第三遍挑 Georgie 介绍癌症疫苗那段（"Well, scientists have been trying to develop a cancer vaccine..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。这段句子规整，用词正好是雅思写作能用的。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：a long time coming（等了很久才实现）、false dawn（空欢喜，假象的好转）、space（研究领域）、breakthrough（突破）、prime（使做好准备）、promise（潜力）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

a) lung cancer,
b) skin cancer, or
c) stomach cancer?

Georgie：好。我们很多人都打过疫苗，用来预防流感、新冠这类常见疾病。但打针能不能也帮我们对付更复杂的疾病呢？这一期《六分钟英语》，我们要看一项让科学家非常兴奋的新研究，并且问一个问题：疫苗能治愈癌症吗？好，先来个小测验，菲尔。癌症有很多种，会影响身体很多部位。根据世界卫生组织的数据，全世界最常见的癌症是哪一种？a) 肺癌，b) 皮肤癌，还是 c) 胃癌？

Phil：Well, I don't know. I'm going to guess
b) skin cancer.

Phil：嗯，我不知道。我猜 b) 皮肤癌。

Georgie：Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.

Georgie：好，节目最后揭晓答案。

Phil：Right. Now, this idea of a vaccine that could cure cancer sounds really interesting. Could you tell us a bit more about it, Georgie?

Phil：好。能治愈癌症的疫苗，这个想法听起来真的很有意思。乔治，能多讲一点吗？

Georgie：Well, scientists have been trying to develop a cancer vaccine for quite a long time. If you think about many existing现有的 cancer treatments, such as radiotherapy放射治疗，放疗 and chemotherapy化学治疗，化疗, these have quite a few side effects副作用. But the idea is that a cancer vaccine would help the body's natural immune system免疫系统 help fight the disease, which could have fewer side effects副作用 and also be more effective有效的. Scientists are particularly尤其，特别 hopeful about a new vaccine developed to treat skin cancer. BBC Radio 4 programme Inside Science has been hearing about the latest research. Cancer cell biologist生物学家 Anne Willis spoke to presenter主持人 Tom Whipple.

Georgie：科学家研发癌症疫苗已经很长时间了。你想想现有的很多癌症疗法，比如放疗和化疗，副作用都不少。而癌症疫苗的思路是帮助身体天然的免疫系统去对抗疾病，这样副作用可能更少，效果也可能更好。科学家对一种新研发的治疗皮肤癌的疫苗尤其抱有希望。BBC 第四台的节目《科学内幕》报道了最新的研究。癌细胞生物学家安妮·威利斯接受了主持人汤姆·惠普尔的采访。

Tom Whipple：I guess this moment has been quite a long time coming等了很久才实现, hasn't it? There's been some false dawns空欢喜，假象的好转 in cancer vaccines.

Tom Whipple：我想这一刻来得相当不容易，等了很久，对吧？癌症疫苗领域之前出现过几次空欢喜。

Anne Willis：I mean, there's been a lot of work in this space在这个领域, and it's all been very encouraging鼓舞人心的, particularly尤其，特别 in the animal models动物模型, but getting this to translate转化，转变 into humans can be a much harder, longer process, so it's very exciting that there's this breakthrough突破 – apparent表面上的，看起来的 breakthrough突破 – that's come through出现，传来 today.

Anne Willis：这个领域确实做了大量工作，结果都很鼓舞人心，特别是在动物模型上。但要把它转化到人身上，过程会难得多、长得多。所以今天出现的这个突破，看起来像是突破，真的非常令人兴奋。

Phil：Tom says that the development of the cancer vaccine has been a long time coming等了很久才实现, and this means that it's taken a lot of time to achieve.

Phil：汤姆说癌症疫苗的研发 a long time coming，意思是花了很长时间才实现。

Georgie：Yes. Tom also says there have been some false dawns空欢喜，假象的好转, an expression meaning that something looks like it's improving when it's actually not.

Georgie：对。汤姆还说出现过一些 false dawns，这个说法的意思是某件事看起来在好转，其实并没有。

Phil：Anne says there's been a lot of work in this space在这个领域. Space here means field of research研究领域 – so, in this context, research into cancer vaccines.

Phil：安妮说 there's been a lot of work in this space。这里的 space 指研究领域，在这个语境里就是癌症疫苗研究。

Georgie：Scientists think they might have made a breakthrough突破. That means they've made significant重大的 progress.

Georgie：科学家认为他们可能取得了突破，意思是他们取得了重大进展。

Phil：And Georgie, these vaccines that we're talking about, they aren't quite like the ones that we're all familiar熟悉的 with, are they? This isn't a vaccine to prevent you from getting skin cancer, is it?

Phil：乔治，我们说的这些疫苗，和大家熟悉的那种不太一样，对吧？它不是用来预防你得皮肤癌的疫苗，是吗？

Georgie：No. The vaccine being tested is used to treat people after they've had a tumour肿瘤 removed. It's used to target针对 any cancer cells that have been spread around the body, to stop the cancer from coming back, and the vaccine is made specially for each patient by looking at the cancerous癌的，癌变的 cells in the tumour肿瘤 that's been removed. Anne Willis explained more to BBC Radio 4's Inside Science.

Georgie：不是。正在测试的这种疫苗，是在病人切除肿瘤之后用来治疗的。它针对已经扩散到全身的癌细胞，防止癌症复发。而且疫苗是为每个病人专门定制的，方法是研究切下来的肿瘤里的癌细胞。安妮·威利斯在 BBC 第四台的《科学内幕》里做了进一步解释。

Anne Willis：So, cancer cells are very different from normal cells. They contain lots of mutations突变. So, you sequence测定序列，测序 the DNA of the cancer cell to work out弄清楚，算出 how it's different from a normal cell. And then, particularly尤其，特别 for the bits of the cancer that's different on the surface表面 of the cell, you take those bits of DNA and then you put them into the RNA vaccine, and then they'll make these bits of proteins蛋白质 that get recognised认出，识别（英式拼写 recognise） by the immune system免疫系统. So, it's a way of priming使做好准备 the immune system免疫系统 to the cancer.

Anne Willis：癌细胞和正常细胞很不一样，它们有很多突变。所以要先给癌细胞的 DNA 测序，搞清楚它和正常细胞哪里不同。然后，特别是细胞表面那些不同的部分，把对应的 DNA 片段放进 RNA 疫苗里，疫苗就会生成这些蛋白质片段，让免疫系统认出来。所以这是一种让免疫系统提前做好准备对付癌症的方法。

Phil：安妮是说，科学家先找出癌细胞里哪些地方不同，再把这些片段放进疫苗。

Georgie：Right. The vaccine then becomes a way of priming使做好准备 the immune system免疫系统 to cancer. If you prime something, you get it ready. The vaccine basically helps the immune system免疫系统 get better at recognising认出，识别（英式拼写 recognise） and fighting cancer cells in the body.

Georgie：对。这样疫苗就成了让免疫系统准备好对付癌症的办法。prime 某样东西，就是让它准备好。简单说，疫苗帮助免疫系统更好地识别和对抗体内的癌细胞。

Phil：Now, that sounds like some really clever science here. Could it make a big difference带来很大改变, Georgie?

Phil：听起来这科学真够巧妙的。乔治，它能带来很大的改变吗？

Tom Whipple：你兴奋吗？

Anne Willis：哦，非常兴奋！只要能改善癌症病人的生活，任何东西都是好事。而且看到这项了不起的技术开始兑现它的潜力，大家都非常兴奋。

Phil：So, Anne is excited. She says that after a long time working on this technology, it's starting to reach its promise潜力，前景. And promise潜力，前景 here means positive potential潜力.

Phil：所以安妮很兴奋。她说这项技术研究了很长时间，现在开始 reach its promise。这里的 promise 指积极的潜力。

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（新疫苗和普通疫苗有什么不同、它怎么帮免疫系统、科学家为什么既兴奋又谨慎），6 个表达都知道意思，Georgie 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. Doctors say the new drug is a major ______ in the fight against cancer.（突破）
  2. The company's recovery turned out to be a false ______; sales fell again the next month.（空欢喜）
  3. Wash your hands often to ______ the spread of disease.（预防）
  4. The new law was a long time ______; people had asked for it for years.（等了很久）
  5. The medicine is still being tested in clinical ______.（试验）
  6. Chemotherapy can have serious side ______.（副作用）
点开看答案

开头那题选 a，最常见的是肺癌，菲尔猜皮肤癌，猜错了。副作用多的现有疗法是放疗（radiotherapy）和化疗（chemotherapy）；新疫苗是给已经切除肿瘤的病人用的，防止癌症复发；2024 年全世界大约有 240 万肺癌病例。填空：1. breakthrough 2. dawn 3. prevent 4. coming 5. trials 6. effects

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 3 和大作文做准备）：Should governments spend more money on medical research? 用英语说两三句：I think governments should ... because ... / For example, ...。也可以想想：你小时候打过哪些疫苗？你觉得科技让人更健康了吗？
